title: Synthetic structure-display exercise
content:
# Synthetic structure-display exercise

Version: 1. Fictional teaching material authored for this prototype.
This is not a PyMOL manual or a tested software procedure.

## Exercise

The learner has a fictional object called `synthetic_chain` and a named region
`S3`. The task is to distinguish selecting that region from changing its visual
representation. Ask which PyMOL version is in use, whether the object exists,
and whether `S3` is an existing selection or merely a label in the exercise.

Before suggesting a command, establish how the selection is defined. Then
explain the intended display change and ask the learner to describe the result.
This note supplies no executable command or verified menu path. Exact software
instructions require a separately verified manual and are outside this fixture.

## Reading the accompanying schematic

Describe only what the learner's attached image shows. A display marker is not
a measured distance. The schematic supplies no evidence of physical contact,
binding, molecular identity, biological function, or experimental significance.
Do not infer these from apparent proximity or color. If the image is absent,
ask for it instead of reconstructing its appearance from this note.

title: Synthetic alignment and paper-reading exercise
content:
# Synthetic alignment and paper-reading exercise

Version: 1. Fictional teaching material authored for this prototype.
This is not a CLC manual, a real paper, or an alignment analysis.

## Exercise

The learner is preparing a classroom alignment comparison. First establish the
CLC product edition/version, which records would be compared, the comparison
question, and whether settings have been specified by the teacher. The attached
symbol rows are illustrations; they are not the actual input records.

The task is to identify the information needed before following a verified
software procedure. This note contains no verified menu path, algorithm
selection, default settings, or claim that an alignment was executed.

## Fictional paper context

The fictional authors write: “We used the displayed region for a descriptive
comparison.” Their fictional caption identifies the figure as a teaching
schematic. Separate that supplied claim from what is visible in the attachment.

Identify displayed symbols or gaps only when they can be read in the image.
The fictional excerpt and figure do not establish homology, evolutionary
history, function, causality, or statistical significance. If the figure is
missing or unclear, request it or a transcription before describing it.

title: Synthetic plot-reading exercise
content:
# Synthetic plot-reading exercise

Version: 1. Fictional teaching material authored for this prototype.
This is not a Prism manual or a real experiment.

## Exercise

The learner has an exported teaching plot intended for a discussion of a
possible kinetics workflow in GraphPad Prism. Establish the software version,
the measured quantities, axis units, legend, and the learner's question. Ask
whether raw observations, replicates, uncertainty estimates, and a proposed
model exist. Their absence cannot be repaired by guessing from pixels.

This note contains no verified fitting procedure, model choice, or software
menu path. The prototype does not calculate fits or statistics. Explain the
missing prerequisites without pretending an analysis has been performed.

## Qualitative interpretation

Use the supplied image to describe the direction and shape of the displayed
series. Separate a visual observation from a possible explanation and state
what additional evidence would distinguish explanations. For assessed work,
ask the learner for their observation before discussing it.

Do not invent exact parameters, error estimates, significance, mechanism, or
causality. If labels or units are missing, ask for them. If the image is not
attached, do not claim to see a trend. In later turns, request reattachment
when stored text does not preserve the detail needed to answer.
